data.title: Markets Espresso: Aag lage basti me, Indian markets apni masti me - or are they?
data.description:
Hello there, Espresso Lovers! We're back after a week that almost felt as if Dalal Street and Wall Street have exchanged addresses, as Dilip Kumar did in Ram Aur Shyam (1968), Sridevi in Chaalbaaz (1989) and Anil Kapoor in Kishan Kanhaiya (1990)! The discourse was also only surrounding two companies - Nvidia, Anthropic, Nvidia, Anthropic. Almost pendulum-like.

It's not just Bollywood; thinkers of the times also used to get "inspired" from people. The source of inspiration today is Isaac Newton - the bane of our existence in college as Science students, and the trigger behind why, as teenagers, we learnt to hurl expletives! Inspired by his law of Universal Gravitation, some legend decided to come up with "What Goes Up Must Come Down!" Some sources also say that it was Newton himself who said this. Doesn't matter; the line exists, and fits right into the glove of the AI trade.

"Jaane do use, is waqt yeh khudgarzi ke ghode pe sawar barbaadi ke toofan mein udta hua chala ja raha hai... aur aise sawar ko waqt ki thappad aur zamaane ki thokar ke siwa koi nahi rok sakta."

If we put the AI trade on one side from the start of the year till November in one screen, put these immortal lines by the late Kadar Khan on another, and the current state of the AI trade in the third screen, it would make a lot of sense. Two stocks took the KOSPI up in South Korea, we know what happened to that. A clutch of names have taken the US markets to record highs one day after another. The action replay of Korea is now playing out on Wall Street.

The AI unwinding is not entirely unexpected, and not entirely surprising either. The way these stocks rose, some of them had numbers to back them, but once reality set in, the fall had to be equally ferocious, if not more. The sky-high valuations were justifiable earlier because companies claimed they were funding their mega spending plans only with their own cash. Now they are in piles of debt.

Every AI-linked company is doing a debt fundraise. SpaceX just sold debt worth $32 billion yesterday. Some day, somebody will ask the question, right? "Where will you pay all the money off from?" It isn't a gift. It has to be repaid. And at a time when companies are committing to such large sums of money for their capex, where will they find the cash to service their debt? The unwinding had to happen someday; it happened in Korea, happened in Taiwan. For how long would Wall Street be insulated from it?

Jensen Huang had one job to do. Business. His company is the most valuable in the world, he is among the top 10 richest people in the world. Instead, he chose to have affairs. Not one, but many. The revelations has now opened a Pandora's box. Nvidia, from being the cynosure of all eyes has become an Eyesore. Jensen Huang's affairs and subsequent exit has taken the stock to its worst losing streak since the global financial crisis, wiped out nearly $3 trillion worth of investor wealth, and has now subjected the company to multiple subpoenas, congressional hearings, and a potential US FTC investigation on accounting malpractices! Talk about falling off a cliff!

The Fed isn't helping matters either. Actually, it's the Fed officials more than the Fed itself. Everybody knew that interest rates were on the upswing because of the persistently high inflation. But then come officials like Christopher Waller, who use terminology like "we need to shock people" and warn of aggressive rate hikes, the "EXIT" door turns into an "EMERGENCY EXIT". The Dow and the Nasdaq had their worst week since March 2020, the Nasdaq has entered a bear market, while the Dow and S&P 500 have entered a "technical correction!"

Now flip the mirror and turn towards our own markets. If there was an Aag Lage Basti Me, Hum Apni Masti Me example to be given, who better than the Indian stock market to represent that? Korea down, Brazil down, Taiwan down, and now even the US is down. What's up? The Nifty! The dollar is strengthening, but despite that, what's strengthening further? The rupee - Asia's best-performing currency for the month!

The Nifty, in less than a month, from 22,500, is now knocking on the doors of 26,000. Largecap stocks are trying to undo the lack of returns over the last few years in a matter of days. HDFC Bank's last five-year returns - Zero. In November? Up 22%. Reliance Industries, up 18% this month, SBI up 21%, Maruti up 23%, even meme material ITC is up 13%. The biggest of them all? The Nifty Bank, which is in a new day, new record mode. Both the Nifty Bank and the PSU Bank index are up nearly 20% this month and are also set for their best month in years.

But what appears on the surface is that really the case? Are portfolios really feeling good? The largecap rally has caught everyone off guard. People who dumped largecap names, avoided them like the Plague, and aimed to find their fortunes in mid, small and momentum-driven stocks find themselves stuck. The AI trade unwinding has hurt two of its biggest beneficiaries. Sterlite Tech is one, from a record high of ₹1,000-plus, the stock is back at ₹600, a 40% fall from the top. Same for HFCL, which has lost more than ₹100 from its own record high level. MTAR Tech and Kaynes Tech, which have significant retail interest, are not on the list of gainers. In fact, they are not only down for the month, but are significantly down from their peaks as well.

For those who are buyers of Gold, look at the prices now! It almost feels like le lo, le lo, raste ka maal saste me. But hang on. This could not be a worse possible time for those using gold as an investment, and especially those who bought it at higher levels, thinking gold toh hamesha upar hi jaata hai! The US Dollar is stronger, the AI trade is unwinding faster than the speed of light, and the Fed is aiming to tighten rates; it's multiple whammies for the Yellow Metal. From record high levels of nearly $5,600, Gold prices globally have knocked off $2,000 and counting. The Silver story is even more sobbing, put on sad daily soap background music and read this. From record highs of $120-plus, Silver prices are on the verge of breaking below $40 an ounce.

Everything across the globe is now in a sea of red. There is uncertainty all around. But Indian equities are in a quiet little bubble of their own. Only the largecaps. Scratch beneath the surface and you'd see concerns emerge. That's where the problem lies. The bulls would hope that it corrects itself soon, and that the newfound love for India from FIIs (pumped in over ₹1 lakh crore so far in November) is a long-lasting one and not just a hawa ka jhonka that came and passed by. We'll be back next week, telling you all the latest brew, and drumroll, it's a holiday-shortened week as well! Take care of yourselves, enjoy the "potentially long weekend" and make the most of whatever little cool weather we are being blessed with!

data.title: SoftBank’s Son explored $1 trillion buyout of SK Hynix, the Information reports
data.description:
SoftBank Group CEO Masayoshi Son recently approached Wall Street institutions about financing a possible trillion-dollar "buyout" of South Korean memory chip company SK Hynix , the Information reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The Information quoted a SoftBank spokesperson as saying Son was no longer considering such a deal.

“SoftBank explores many opportunities, and this one is no longer under active consideration,” the report said, citing the spokesperson.

SK Hynix said in a statement it has no knowledge of the matter described in the Information report.

It added that any foreign acquisition of the company would require prior government approval under Korean law.

A SoftBank spokesperson referred to the statement the company gave to the Information, when Reuters sought a comment.

data.title: Hong Kong pushes to bring crypto custodians, advisers under licensing rules
data.description:
Hong Kong has published a bill that would bring crypto custodians, advisers and other virtual asset service providers under mandatory licensing or registration, extending oversight beyond trading platforms.

On Friday, the government officially published its Virtual Asset Services Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026, proposing to regulate four activities, including virtual asset dealing, advisory, management and custody. Firms carrying out those activities would need to obtain a license from or register with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC).

The proposed amendments to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance would subject providers to fit-and-proper checks and other regulatory requirements. Banks and stored-value facility licensees supervised by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority would also have to register with the SFC to offer virtual asset services.

SFC chief executive Julia Leung said the proposal would strengthen investor protections and provide clearer paths for responsible innovation. The bill is set for its first reading in the Legislative Council on Dec. 2.

In October, Hong Kong said it would introduce legislation covering those four activities before the end of 2026, following consultations on the proposed framework.

The expanded regime has raised implementation concerns. In January, the Hong Kong Securities & Futures Professionals Association warned that introducing licenses without transitional arrangements could force existing businesses to suspend operations while their applications are reviewed. The association called for a six- to 12-month grace period.

data.title: South Korea's Lee says speed is vital in AI race on data centre visit
data.description:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Saturday urged the country to move fast as it competes in the global AI race, as he toured a data centre under construction in the southeastern city of Ulsan.

"The whole world is competing right now, and speed is vital," Lee said in a public video of his tour.

Data centres are a major source of chip demand, and he hoped the success of the project, built by South Korea's second-largest conglomerate SK Group, would draw further investment from global AI companies, Lee said.

SK Group is developing the Ulsan data centre jointly with Amazon Web Services (AWS). The estimated cost is 7 trillion won ($5.2 billion) until 2029, South Korea's science ministry said last year. Operations are scheduled to begin in the second half of 2027.

SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won said in September that the capacity under construction was an initial 103 megawatt by 2029, with plans to expand it by nearly 900 megawatts in the future. The group is also planning further partnerships with global technology companies as the project progresses, Chey said.

On Saturday, President Lee said AI investment had mainly been concentrated around Seoul, and that the Ulsan project showed regional growth was possible.

After being told that about 900 people were working at the site, Lee said advanced facilities were short of construction workers and that ministries needed to consider how to train the workforce for building data centres and AI infrastructure.

($1 = 1,343.3600 won)

data.title: IndusInd Bank ends ex-CEO Kathpalia's employment, seeks to recover pay
data.description:
IndusInd Bank said on Friday, November 20, it has terminated former top boss Sumant Kathpalia's employment with the bank and is seeking to recover pay spanning his entire tenure, following a disciplinary inquiry.

Kathpalia resigned in April 2025 after IndusInd Bank disclosed incorrect accounting on derivative trades that prompted a $230 million hit to its accounts, throwing the private-sector lender into a crisis that hit its shares and drew regulatory scrutiny.

The bank told Kathpalia he would remain in employment and then initiated disciplinary proceedings against him. In June 2025 he was suspended, pending completion of the proceedings.

Based on the findings of an inquiry report this week, the bank's board decided to terminate Kathpalia's employment and invoke applicable malus and clawback provisions with effect from the date of his initial appointment as CEO in March 2020.

IndusInd did not disclose details of the inquiry's findings. Reuters could not reach Kathpalia for comment.

Reuters had reported in November 2025 that the lender had begun a process to claw back salary and bonuses from Kathpalia and former deputy CEO Arun Khurana, after an internal review flagged misconduct and misreporting.

Indian banking regulations have allowed clawback provisions in employee contracts since 2019 to deter misconduct, but such efforts have been rare.

IndusInd's loans and deposits returned to double-digit growth in the second quarter of the current fiscal year, the first time since the accounting discrepancies emerged. Its shares are up 16% this year after dropping 10% in 2025.

data.description:
Tezos artists will have until November 28th to submit Genesis mints from Hic et Nunc or Teia for a December exhibition at the Teia Community Centre in Decentraland.

Refer to the official tweet by XTZ:

Tezos
@tezos

Art on Tezos Friday Recap 🔔

â†’ objkt and Wintercircus 📍 Ghent launched PUBLIC DISPLAY, a series of solo exhibitions on the venue's LED wall. On view is "I Think You're Testing Me" by @malpractice_net, curated by @_second_guess with @artontezos_, November 19â€“25, followed byâ€¦ pic.twitter.com/hfMYLKW681

Nov 20, 2026

XTZ Info

Tezos is a distinctive blockchain platform architected to facilitate and govern decentralized applications (dApps) and smart contracts. Its foundation is built on a decentralized governance system that enables blockchain modifications through a community-led decision-making process.

Operating on a unique iteration of Proof of Stake (PoS) mechanism known as Liquid Proof of Stake (LPoS), Tezos allows participants owning more than 6,000 Tez (XTZ) to become delegates, or “bakers”. These bakers are responsible for creating, signing, and publishing new blocks on the Tezos blockchain, and endorsing blocks produced by other bakers. Furthermore, the network utilizes the Michelson programming language for the creation of smart contracts, which engage with the network’s cryptocurrency, Tez, for transaction execution and gas payment.

The native token of Tezos, XTZ, or Tez, plays a multifaceted role within the ecosystem. It serves as a reward for participation in the creation and endorsement of new blocks, either directly or through delegation. It functions as a voting mechanism within the decentralized governance system. Additionally, it is a means of value transfer and is used to pay for gas, the unit of computational effort in Tezos, necessary for executing transactions and interacting with smart contracts.

data.title: Crypto News Today: Bitcoin Price Nears $55K as Ethereum Plunges 10% and XRP Tests $0.87 Support
data.description:
The November 21 selloff has kept all three cryptocurrencies under pressure, with moving averages indicating sustained bearish momentum. Although oversold readings suggest that selling pressure could ease temporarily, the broader technical picture remains negative. Investors are watching whether Bitcoin can stabilize below $60,000, Ethereum can defend the $1,550–$1,580 area, and XRP can avoid another test of its recent lows.

Bitcoin Price Nears $55K as Bearish Signals Strengthen

Bitcoin (BTC) remains under significant selling pressure after falling below $60,000 for the first time since July. Reuters reported that BTC declined 9.67% to $55,809 at 03:50 GMT on November 21. The latest move followed a broader retreat in risk assets, with concerns about elevated valuations weighing on the artificial intelligence trade and other market segments.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The technical picture also points to continued weakness. The TradingView recorded 16 sell signals, seven neutral readings, and only three buy signals across its combined indicators. Moving averages were particularly bearish, with 14 sell signals, one neutral reading, and no buy signals. This alignment suggests that Bitcoin's downtrend extends beyond a short-term price correction.

Several momentum indicators reinforce that assessment. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) on the 14-day setting stood at 18, indicating deeply oversold conditions. The Commodity Channel Index (CCI) reached -127, while Williams Percent Range fell to -93. These readings suggest that selling may be approaching exhaustion, although they do not independently establish a price reversal.

Meanwhile, the MACD remained negative at -5,033, and the Momentum indicator registered -15,050. Both readings point to persistent downward pressure. The Average Directional Index (ADX) at 46 also indicates a strong prevailing trend, supporting the view that the bearish structure remains firmly established.

Bitcoin's moving averages provide further evidence of the weakness. The 10-day exponential and simple moving averages stood near $64,088 and $64,125, respectively. Longer-term averages were positioned considerably higher, with the 50-day EMA near $73,842 and the 200-day EMA around $75,217. These levels represent potential recovery barriers if buyers attempt to regain control.

The supplied classic pivot analysis identified $58,181 as an important support reference. However, with the later Bitcoin quote already below that level, traders need to reassess the pivot structure against updated price data. On the upside, the $64,000 area represents an initial resistance zone based on the short-term moving averages.

Ethereum Price Plunges Over 10% as $1,543 Support Comes Into Focus

Ethereum (ETH) experienced an even sharper decline, with one CoinGlass market snapshot showing the cryptocurrency at $1,543.46, down 10.69% over 24 hours. Its recorded intraday range extended from $1,539.90 to $1,762.80. A subsequent market update showed ETH recovering toward $1,618, illustrating how quickly prices have moved during the selloff.

Ethereum (ETH) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The TradingView technical classified Ethereum's overall position as Strong Sell. The combined indicator summary recorded 16 sell signals and 10 neutral readings, with no buy signals. Moving averages accounted for 14 sell signals and one neutral reading, while the oscillator group remained predominantly neutral.

Ethereum's momentum indicators also reflect the scale of the decline. The 14-day RSI stood at 18.9, placing it well below the traditional oversold threshold of 30. The Stochastic %K reached 6.8, while the CCI registered -133.8. These readings indicate substantial downward pressure and the possibility of a temporary recovery if selling activity slows.

However, the MACD at -170.8 and Momentum indicator at -450.1 continued to generate sell signals. The ADX reading of 41.7 suggests that the prevailing trend remains strong rather than reflecting ordinary sideways price movement. As a result, the oversold readings have not yet provided sufficient confirmation of a bullish reversal.

Ethereum is also trading considerably below its key moving averages. The 10-day EMA and SMA stood near $1,833 and $1,838, respectively, while the 20-day EMA was positioned around $1,975. The 50-day EMA near $2,181 and 200-day EMA around $2,262 highlight the distance ETH would need to recover before its broader technical structure begins to improve.

The $1,550–$1,580 area is an important near-term zone to monitor, given the recent trading range. A sustained move below this region could expose Ethereum to further losses. Conversely, the Hull Moving Average near $1,697 represents an initial recovery hurdle, followed by resistance around the $1,833–$1,838 moving-average cluster.

XRP Price Tests $0.87 Support as Oversold Readings Emerge

XRP (XRP) has also experienced persistent selling, with the price falling below the $1.00 level and approaching an important technical support region. A previous technical snapshot placed XRP near $0.8710, while subsequent market data showed the token recovering toward $0.91. Its November 20 trading session recorded a low around $0.865, keeping the $0.87 support zone in focus.

XRP price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The broader trend remains bearish despite some improvements in short-term momentum readings. The TradingView daily technical showed a Sell rating, while the hourly, four-hour, and weekly timeframes also leaned toward Sell or Strong Sell. This reflects the pressure affecting XRP across multiple trading periods.

The 14-day RSI stood near 25.42, indicating oversold conditions. The Stochastic %K was around 11.97, while Williams Percent Range reached approximately -92.46. These readings suggest that XRP has experienced substantial selling and could enter a consolidation phase if buyers return.

However, its moving averages continue to indicate a weak market structure. The 10-day simple moving average was near $0.9618, while the corresponding exponential average stood around $0.9727. Longer-term averages were positioned substantially higher, including the 50-day SMA near $1.24 and the 100-day SMA around $1.31.

The MACD and Momentum indicators also remained negative, highlighting the difference between short-term oversold conditions and the broader downward trend.

Classic pivot calculations identify $0.8718 as the first notable support level, followed by $0.8343 and $0.7469. On the upside, the central pivot sits near $0.9217, with initial resistance around $0.9592. A sustained move above these levels would help reduce immediate bearish pressure, while a break below $0.8718 could expose XRP to additional selling.

Crypto Market Outlook: Oversold Conditions Face Persistent Selling Pressure

Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP are displaying similar technical characteristics despite differences in their recent price movements. All three assets are trading below their principal moving averages, while negative MACD and momentum readings continue to indicate downward pressure.

The oversold readings across their RSI and other oscillators deserve attention. Bitcoin's RSI near 18, Ethereum's at 18.9, and XRP's around 25.42 suggest that recent selling has pushed momentum toward historically weak territory. Such conditions can precede a temporary rebound, but they do not guarantee that prices have reached a durable bottom.

The key distinction is that moving averages continue to favor sellers. Bitcoin faces recovery barriers beginning around $64,000, Ethereum must reclaim levels near $1,697 and $1,833, while XRP needs to move above its $0.92–$0.96 resistance region to improve its short-term outlook.

For now, the immediate focus remains on price stabilization. Bitcoin's ability to recover above $60,000, Ethereum's response around $1,550, and XRP's defense of the $0.87 region will help determine whether the current decline begins to slow or develops into another leg lower.

The technical readings reflect historical price behavior and can change quickly as new trading data becomes available. Until stronger buying activity and confirmation across multiple timeframes emerge, the broader market structure continues to favor a cautious outlook.

data.description:
The latest BSE index reshuffle will also see Divi’s Laboratories replace Wipro in the Sensex 50, while five companies each will be added to and removed from the BSE 100

Shriram Finance will replace Trent in the 30-stock BSE Sensex from 21 December, following a reconstitution of several benchmark indices announced by BSE Index Services on Friday.

The changes, which will take effect at the opening of trading on 21 December, will also affect the BSE 100, BSE Sensex 50, BSE Sensex Next 50, BSE Sensex Next 30 and BSE Focused IT indices.

Changes In Key Indices

In the BSE Sensex 50, Divi’s Laboratories will replace information technology services company Wipro. The BSE 100 will see five additions and five exclusions. Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX), Vedanta Aluminium Metal, Laurus Labs, Bharat Heavy Electricals (BHEL) and GE Vernova T&D India will enter the index.

They will replace Punjab National Bank, Godrej Consumer Products, SRF, Shree Cement and Havells India, respectively. The BSE Sensex Next 50 will also undergo six changes. MCX, Vedanta Aluminium Metal, Laurus Labs, BHEL, GE Vernova T&D India and Wipro will be included, replacing Divi’s Laboratories, Havells India, Godrej Consumer Products, Shree Cement, SRF and Punjab National Bank.

Rejig Across Other Indices

The BSE Sensex Next 30 will see Trent, Adani Power, Federal Bank, MCX and Cummins India enter the index. They will replace Britannia Industries, HDFC Life Insurance, Suzlon Energy, Wipro and Shriram Finance.

In the BSE Focused IT index, Sagility will replace L&T Technology Services. The BSE Bankex will remain unchanged in the latest review.

The periodic reconstitution of indices is intended to ensure that their composition reflects changes in market representation, liquidity and free-float market capitalisation. Such changes can also require index-tracking funds and exchange-traded funds to realign their portfolios.

data.title: IoTeX Opened Voting on IIP-65 Bunker Mode
data.description:
IoTeX opened voting on IIP-65, “Bunker Mode”, on November 21st at 00:00 UTC; voting will continue until November 28th at 00:00 UTC. The proposal would add an optional SLH-DSA guard key to staked IOTX, preventing withdrawals, transfers and voting changes without that key while staking rewards continue.

Refer to the official tweet by IOTX:

IoTeX
@iotex_io

Voting on IIP-65: Bunker Mode 🛡ï¸ opens today at 4pm PT (00:00 UTC, Nov 21).

Nobody knows when a quantum computer, or an AI-assisted math breakthrough, will break the ECDSA keys that protect crypto today. Upgrading every account to post-quantum needs exchanges, wallets andâ€¦

Nov 20, 2026

IOTX Info

IoTeX (IOTX) is an open-source blockchain platform specifically designed for the Internet of Things (IoT) with a strong emphasis on scalability, privacy, isolation, and the ability to develop decentralized applications and IoT ecosystems.

IoTeX was created to address the technical challenges faced by existing IoT ecosystems, such as security issues, high maintenance costs, and scalability limitations. The project is developing a new blockchain architecture to support a large number of IoT devices.

At the core of IoTeX is the concept of "blockchain within a blockchain." The main network, or "root blockchain," is responsible for network management and security, while internal blockchains, or "sub-blockchains," are used to manage various IoT devices and process transactions.

The IoTeX network utilizes its native token, IOTX, for operations such as transaction fee payments and participation in network governance.

data.title: BENQI to Introduce an sAVAX Unstaking Queue in November
data.description:
BENQI will update sAVAX unstaking in November, replacing the fixed 15-day wait with a queue following Avalanche’s Helicon upgrade. AVAX, including accrued rewards, could become available in as little as 48 hours or take up to 14 days during high demand; existing requests will carry over with elapsed waiting time preserved.

Refer to the official tweet by QI:

BENQI🔺
@BenqiFinance

2/2 Holding sAVAX? You donâ€™t need to move or swap it. Your sAVAX remains the same and still earns staking rewards automatically.

Already unstaking? Your request will carry over, and the time youâ€™ve already waited still counts. Once your AVAX is ready, you can claim it anytime.â€¦

Nov 20, 2026

QI Info

BENQI is a DeFi protocol developed on the Avalanche network, comprising two main components: BENQI Liquid Staking (BLS) and BENQI Liquidity Market (BLM). BLS provides a liquid staking solution for Avalanche, allowing users to earn yields on staked capital, while BLM facilitates a lending and borrowing environment for crypto-assets through smart contracts.

The operational mechanism of BENQI involves BLS, which enables users to stake with Avalanche validators and use the staked assets without lock-up periods. BLM, on the other hand, operates as a lending and borrowing protocol on the Avalanche network, allowing users to lend, borrow, and earn interest on their crypto assets. The protocol is fully automated through smart contracts, calculating yields algorithmically based on supply and demand, and enabling over-collateralized borrowing.

QI is the native token of BENQI, serving dual roles as a governance and utility token. It is essential for managing and voting on proposals within the BENQI DAO, influencing the protocol’s direction, including economic policies, security upgrades, and further development. Additionally, QI allows for staking, earning delegation rewards, and provides enhanced functionality within the BENQI ecosystem.

data.title: Anthropic's 20X Sales Valuation Makes Samsung And Hynix Look Like Bargains, Warns Dan Niles
data.description:
Key points:
  • Niles said that he attempted to short Anthropic after the stock surged roughly 30% following its IPO, but was unable to find shares available to borrow.
  • He noted that for him, the comparison comes down to how much investors are paying for exposure to the broader AI ecosystem and the risks embedded in those valuations.
  • Anthropic shares opened 34% higher on debut and finished the session up 17%, a performance Niles said was less convincing than the headline gains might suggest.

Anthropic's blockbuster IPO has put the artificial intelligence trade back in the spotlight, but veteran tech investor Dan Niles questioned whether investors are paying too steep a price for the AI startup's growth prospects.

During an interview with CNBC, Niles said he sees a stark valuation contrast between Anthropic and established semiconductor players like Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. (SSNLF) and SK Hynix Inc. (SKHY), arguing that investors betting on AI may be overlooking more attractively priced opportunities elsewhere in the ecosystem.

Anthropic shares fell nearly 9% in Friday’s regular trading, declining over 1% more during the afterhours session.

Niles Says He Tried To Short ANT Stock As Its Shares Surged

Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, said that he attempted to short Anthropic after the stock surged roughly 30% following its IPO, but was unable to find shares available to borrow.

"When it was up 30% yesterday, I went and tried to get a borrow to short it. There was none available. I tried, I tried again this morning to get a borrow to short it. There was none available," Niles said during an appearance on CNBC's Squawk on the Street on Thursday.

Niles questioned whether Anthropic's valuation justified the enthusiasm, contrasting the company's valuation with those of established semiconductor companies that are also benefiting from the AI infrastructure boom.

"You can buy it at 20 times trailing revenues or calendar 26 revenues, or you could go buy Samsung or Hynix at two times trailing earnings," he said.

Niles noted that for him, the comparison comes down to how much investors are paying for exposure to the broader AI ecosystem and the risks embedded in those valuations.

He emphasized that investing ultimately comes down to weighing potential returns against the risks involved, with valuations offering a crucial gauge of that balance.

Niles Questions Whether Anthropic's IPO Was As Successful As It Appeared

Anthropic's IPO initially appeared to deliver a strong debut, with shares opening substantially higher before giving back some of those gains by the close. Niles, however, argued that the intraday price action raised questions about the strength of demand relative to selling pressure.

The stock opened 34% higher and finished the session up 17%, a performance Niles said was less convincing than the headline gains might suggest.

"You can make an argument that the IPO did not go that great," Niles said.

While he acknowledged that the offering was positive for Anthropic itself because the company raised more money than expected, he pointed to the gap between the opening and closing gains as a potential warning sign.

"For a successful IPO you want to see it open and then continue to climb during the day," Niles said.

"It opened up 34%. It closed up 17. So what does that tell you?"

Niles said the price action suggested sellers were more aggressive at the open than buyers looking to enter the stock, raising doubts about whether Anthropic could sustain its IPO price.

"Clearly the sellers were more aggressive at the open versus anybody who wanted to step into it," he said.

Ultimately, Niles returned to the valuation question, arguing that investors need to weigh the price they are paying for AI exposure against alternatives in the semiconductor industry.

"If you don't want to buy Samsung at three times earnings, do you really want to buy this at 20 times sales? That's the problem."

What Retail Investors Think Of ANT Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Anthropic trended in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

ANT stock is down 20% year-to-date. The S&P 500 ETF (SPY) is up 6% over the past 12 months, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is up 4%.

data.title: Star Atlas to Deploy SAGE C4 3.2 PTR Update on November 21st
data.description:
Star Atlas will deploy the SAGE C4 3.2 PTR update for its browser game Golden Era on November 21st. The update will revise Council research and career progression, add governance modules and voting at eligible starbases, and rebalance ship configurations, regional resources and crafting.

Refer to the official tweet by ATLAS:

Star Atlas
@staratlas

The single largest update to Star Atlas: Golden Era (browser), ever. Going live today.

SAGE C4 3.2 PTR â€” PATCH NOTES

Council progression, ship fitting, territorial governance, resource distribution, and more. The release review covered 390 pull requests.

COUNCIL RANK &â€¦ pic.twitter.com/tMrdf1CoGy

Nov 21, 2026

ATLAS Info

Star Atlas is an ambitious MMO game built on the Solana blockchain. It serves as a true metaverse, combining elements of strategy, exploration, and combat in a world filled with cosmic science fiction.

Star Atlas offers players the opportunity to explore space, mine resources, build ships and colonies, and engage in battles with other players. The in-game economy is based on cryptocurrencies, enabling players to earn real money through their participation in the game. Every action, from resource mining to construction and battles, can be tokenized and exchanged for real-world currency.

Star Atlas utilizes non-fungible tokens (NFTs) to create unique digital assets that can be traded on its in-game marketplace. These NFTs encompass a wide range of items, including spaceships and land plots on various planets.

By leveraging the scalability and low fees of the Solana blockchain, Star Atlas establishes a seamless, dynamic, and immersive gaming environment. Additionally, the project incorporates Unreal Engine 5 technology to craft a visually detailed game world.

The ATLAS token serves as the in-game currency within the Star Atlas metaverse. It is a cryptocurrency that players can utilize for various purposes within the game.

data.title: Gold made investors richer. But could their money have worked harder?
data.description:
Gold is one of the few assets Indians buy without first asking what it will return. We buy it for weddings, festivals and family security. For generations, it has symbolised wealth preservation and financial protection.

So, when gold prices rise sharply, it creates a perception that everyone holding gold has become wealthier. But there is a difference between an asset performing well and investors actually capturing those returns.

After an extraordinary rally followed by a sharp correction, three questions matter: When did investors buy gold? What drove returns in India? And what opportunities did they give up by choosing gold over other investments?

Gold went up. Did investors capture the rally?

Between March 2024 and October 2026, Gold ETFs attracted cumulative net inflows of Rs 1.01 lakh crore. Interestingly, nearly 50 percent came during 2026, after gold had already appreciated substantially.

To understand the impact, we compared actual investor cash flows with two hypothetical approaches involving the same cumulative investment of Rs 1,01,397 crore.

The annualised return on actual investor flows was just 15.50 percent. Investing a fixed amount every month would have delivered 29.70 percent, while investing the entire amount at the beginning would have generated 32.72 percent.

The difference is striking. Despite gold's extraordinary rally, investors captured considerably lower returns because of when they invested.

This reflects recency bias. Investors often become more comfortable buying an asset after watching its price rise. The lesson is not that lump sum investing always outperforms SIPs, but that investment decisions should follow a disciplined allocation strategy rather than recent performance.

Why does gold deliver different returns in India?

International gold prices are denominated in US dollars, but Indian households buy gold in rupees. Domestic returns, therefore, depend on global prices, currency movements and import duties.

Our analysis of the past 20 years shows that gold delivered average annual returns of 11.92 percent in dollar terms, compared with 16.05 percent in rupees. The 4.13 percentage-point difference is largely attributable to rupee depreciation.

A recent one-year period illustrates this particularly well. International gold prices declined 5.40 percent, yet Indian prices rose 10.23 percent. This divergence of 15.63 percentage points was largely driven by 7 percent rupee depreciation and an increase in customs duty from 6 percent to 15 percent.

But can this additional return continue indefinitely? Not necessarily. A stronger rupee or lower import duties could put pressure on domestic gold prices even if international prices remain unchanged.

What else could that money have earned?

The more interesting question is not just how much wealth gold created, but whether the same money could have earned more elsewhere.

Our analysis estimates that Indian households invested Rs 118.97 lakh crore in gold between 2013 and 2026. At November 2026 valuations, this would have grown to Rs 464.99 lakh crore.

However, investing the equivalent amount in the equity mutual fund basket used in our comparison would have generated Rs 554.42 lakh crore, nearly Rs 90 lakh crore more.

This does not mean households literally lost Rs 90 lakh crore. It is a hypothetical comparison. Gold bought for weddings, jewellery and family requirements serves purposes that equities cannot replace.

Nevertheless, it highlights an important distinction: earning positive returns is not necessarily the same as maximising wealth creation. Every investment choice carries an opportunity cost.

The recent correction: What has changed?

After an extraordinary rally, international gold prices have fallen nearly 31 percent from their January 2026 peak of $5,405 per ounce, while domestic prices have corrected 25 percent from Rs 1,75,231 per 10 grams.

Concerns over US inflation and tighter monetary policy have increased the attractiveness of interest-bearing investments. The US 10-year Treasury yield has crossed 5 percent, while a stronger dollar has added pressure on gold.

Investor behaviour has also contributed. Momentum-driven buying and leveraged positions during the rally gave way to profit booking and the unwinding of futures positions as prices declined.

Demand is moderating, too. Global jewellery consumption fell 17 percent year-on-year in Q3 2026, while Indian consumption declined 20 percent. Global Gold ETF inflows slowed from $10 billion in September to $2.7 billion in October.

The correction does not mean gold has lost its long-term relevance. But it reinforces a familiar lesson: past performance cannot be extrapolated indefinitely, and a sharp price decline does not automatically make an investment attractive.

Should gold be part of every investor's portfolio?

As a broad allocation framework, investors can consider allocating up to 50 percent of their debt allocation to gold, or 10–15 percent of their overall portfolio. Those already overweight on gold should consider rebalancing towards their strategic allocation rather than adding exposure simply because prices have corrected.

The objective of investing is not to own whichever asset has delivered the highest recent returns. It is to build a portfolio that offers the highest probability of achieving financial goals.

Ultimately, the real measure of wealth creation is not how brightly an asset shines, but how effectively it contributes to an investor's overall financial journey.

The author is the Joint CEO Anand Rathi Wealth Limited.
